subject: Anthropology
title: Religion and Globalization
description: A quick, practical guide to Religion and Globalization.

hook.text: Yoga studios in New York. Evangelical megachurches in Nigeria. Buddhism apps in London. Religion has gone global.

buildup.text: Globalization spreads religious ideas, practices, and movements across borders faster than ever before in history.

discovery.text: Pentecostalism is the fastest-growing religious movement — spreading from the US to Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

twist.text: Global religions adapt locally. African Pentecostalism looks different from American — same faith, new local forms.

climax.text: Globalization doesn't create one world religion. It creates hybrid forms — local traditions reshaped by global flows.

punchline.text: Religion goes global; the local makes it its own.

quiz.question: How does globalization affect religion?
options: It creates one unified world religion
It spreads religions that then adapt to local contexts

details.summary: Globalization both threatens and energizes religion. It spreads religions to new territories, creates hybrid spiritual practices, and provokes fundamentalist reactions against cultural homogenization while connecting religious communities across unprecedented distances.
details.whyItMatters: Religion in a globalized world is more dynamic, diverse, and politically significant than secularization theorists predicted. Understanding religious globalization is crucial for making sense of contemporary cultural and political conflicts.
takeaways: Globalization spreads religions and creates hybrid spiritual practices
It also provokes fundamentalist reactions against cultural change
Religious globalization shapes contemporary politics and culture

faq.question: How does globalization create new forms of religion?
faq.answer: Migration brings religions into contact, producing syncretic blends. The internet enables global spiritual communities. Yoga becomes exercise in the West. Pentecostalism adapts to local cultures across Africa and Latin America. Globalization creates constant religious innovation.

faq.question: Why does globalization sometimes strengthen fundamentalism?
faq.answer: When globalization threatens local cultures and identities, religious fundamentalism provides a framework for resistance. It offers certainty in uncertain times, community in fragmented societies, and clear identity against the homogenizing forces of global culture.
